newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA debt off on weak Dec retail sales.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA debt off on weak Dec retail sales.

text.p: CompUSA Inc debt dropped a full point on Wednesday in sympathy with the firm's stock, which tumbled 4-3/4 points, on a weaker-than-expected December same store sales report, corporate bond traders said.
"CompUSA's 9.50 (percent) paper due 2000 was quoted off a point at 102-1/4 bid, 102-3/8 offer, on the board," one trader said.

News the computer retailer reported a disappointing 1.5 percent gain in December same store sales triggered declines in the firm's debt and equity, traders said. CompUSA's stock slid 4-3/4 points to trade at 15-7/8 since the news hit.

CompUSA Inc chief executive officer, James Halpin, told Reuters in an interview he was "not happy" with sluggish Christmas retail sales, but forecast the release of Intel Corp's new multimedia chip in January would bring better business.
Halpin thought Christmas sales were slow because customers preferred to wait for the January 8 introduction of Intel's new multimedia MMX chip before upgrading their computers.

Reflecting a broad slump in home computer sales, Tandy Corp said earlier in the week that it would sell all 17 Incredible Universe superstores and shut 19 of its 108 Computer City stores in North America.
Tandy said stiff competition had taken a toll on the enormous stores, which offer a full range of consumer electronic goods.
In addition, Best Buy Co, one of the country's largest retailers of electronics, personal computers and appliances, last month reported its first quarterly loss in over a decade.
